e-Flora of South AfricaMorphology

Perennial herb, geophyte, 0.6-1.5 m high; corm tunics brown, coarsely reticulate; stem inclined below, simple. Leaves lanceolate to linear, 10-18 mm wide, margins and midrib thickened. Bracts strongly imbricate, dry and brownish, apiculate to attenuate, inner apically forked. Inflorescence a dense spike; flowers pink, rarely white, with dark pink streak in lower midline of each tepal, nearly bilabiate; tepals broadly lanceolate, apiculate; upper 3 ascending; lower horizontal. Spike densely 30- to 42-flowered, internodes 4-6(-8) mm long; bracts dry and brown, often greenish straw-coloured with darker brown margins, with evident pale netted veins, 22-25(-28) mm long, clasping stem in lower half, strongly overlapping, apiculate to attenuate, inner shorter and concealed, forked apically for at least 2 mm. Flowers zygomorphic, weakly bilabiate, bright pink (rarely white), often with darker median streak in basal half of tepals; perianth tube with lower part 12-18 mm long, upper part ascending and funnel-shaped, 9-12 mm long, 8 mm diam. at mouth; tepals lanceolate, 18-24 x 7-9 mm, upper three spreading and lower three nearly horizontal. Filaments unilateral and arcuate, 10-12 mm long, included in tube; anthers 9-11 mm long, whitish to mauve or violet. Style arching over stamens, dividing near anther apices, branches ± 6 mm long. Capsules narrowly ovoid, 10-12 mm long. Seeds elongate-angular, with rudimentary distal and proximal wings, 4-5 x 2 mm.

Habitat

In well-watered, open grassy slopes. Sub-Escarpment Grassland, Sub-Escarpment Savanna, Indian Ocean Coastal Belt. Open grassy slopes, usually in well-watered sites. Open grassy slopes, usually in well-watered sites.

Diagnostic Description

Distinguished from other species with dense spikes of moderate-sized, pink, funnel-shaped flowers and coarse, dry, brown, overlapping bracts by its densely clumped habit, with the stems inclined at the base and then sharply erect below the spike. The bracts are greenish straw-coloured with noticeably darker brown margins and pale venation. Watsonia canaliculata has similar pale bracts but is a solitary-growing species with erect stems and channelled leaves; W. pulchra has dark brown bracts and broad leaves, (10-)15-30 mm wide with heavily thickened margins; and W. lepida is a shorter, solitary-growing species, with the lowermost leaves dry and broken at flowering, and uniformly dark brown bracts.

Distribution

Widely distributed along the East Coast and near interior South Africa, from Port St Johns in Eastern Cape to St Lucia Bay in northern KwaZulu-Natal, extending inland to Dundee.
